title: About Chikungunya Virus

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Chikungunya is a disease caused by a virus spread by infected mosquitoes. Outbreaks of chikungunya virus have occurred in Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe, and islands in the Indian and Pacific Oceans. There is a risk the virus can spread to unaffected areas by infected travelers.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.text: The most common symptoms of chikungunya are fever and joint pain. Other symptoms can include headache, muscle pain, joint swelling, or rash.

sections.heading: How it spreads
sections.text: Chikungunya virus spreads to people through the bites of infected mosquitoes. During the first week of illness, people sick with chikungunya can spread the virus to uninfected mosquitoes.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.text: The best way to prevent chikungunya is to protect yourself from mosquito bites. Vaccination is recommended for some travelers.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.text: If you have chikungunya, prevent mosquito bites for the first week of your illness to avoid spreading virus to uninfected mosquitoes.

sections.heading: Testing and diagnosis
sections.text: See your healthcare provider if you have symptoms after visiting an area at risk for chikungunya virus.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.text: No medicines are available to treat chikungunya. Rest, fluids, and over-the-counter pain medicines can relieve some symptoms.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.text: Take medicine such as acetaminophen or paracetamol to reduce fever and pain.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.text: Do not take aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS), such as ibuprofen, until dengue can be ruled out to reduce the risk of bleeding.

sections.heading: Treatment
sections.text: For healthcare providers: Treatment and Prevention of Chikungunya Virus Disease
